plan.title: Liver treated vs control: descriptive DE (no replicates)
plan.analytical_narrative: The data profile shows one treated liver sample and one control liver sample, raw salmon gene counts (12000 genes x 3 columns incl. gene symbol) with zero biological replication in either arm. The design-knowledge service flags this design explicitly (rule R-0003): without within-group replication, DESeq2 cannot estimate a dispersion, so no p-value from a two-sample comparison carries an inferential basis. The plan runs the standard bulk RNA-seq pipeline up to and including normalization, then substitutes a descriptive fold-change report for the usual inferential test. Steps: (1) QC on sample structure; (2) low-count filtering at min_samples=1 (smallest group size); (3) DESeq2 median-of-ratios normalization; (4) a descriptive log2 fold-change table with apeglm shrinkage, explicitly withholding any inferential test per the flagged rule; (5) GO biological-process over-representation analysis (clusterProfiler enrichGO + rrvgo redundancy reduction) on genes screened by fold-change magnitude, using the tested-gene universe -- chosen because the knowledge-check rejected fgsea/Hallmark preranked GSEA for this exact flagged, replicate-free situation and named GO-ORA with clusterProfiler as the permitted alternative; (6) a reproducibility report stating the design limitation, thresholds, versions, and session info up front.

steps.method: DESeq2 vst(blind), PCA, sample distance heatmap, library sizes
Keep genes with >=10 counts in at least 1 sample (smallest group size)
Descriptive log2 fold changes only, no inferential test (no replication)
apeglm shrinkage of the treated-vs-control log2 fold change
fgsea preranked GSEA on descriptive log2 fold change vs MSigDB Hallmark, then Reactome
Reproducible report with session info, thresholds, descriptive DE table, enrichment tables
GO over-representation with clusterProfiler enrichGO and rrvgo term reduction (descriptive gene list, no inferential DE test available)
